Les Hilarious Riders est un club de moto: The Hilarious Riders is an activist motorcycle club rooted in the community and in Black youth in Montréal and beyond.
Le groupe Hilarious Riders. Crédit photo: The Hilarious Riders group. Photo credit: Ismaël Koné
Le reportage que vous vous apprêtez à li: The story you’re about to read is about a motorcycle club that is involved in the community. I’m a motorcyclist myself. Over the years, I’ve owned a few Japanese sport bikes. In the past, I sometimes had the idea of doing a story that would let me write about this world I’m passionate about, but I couldn’t find a subject strong enough to do it. That is, until I heard about the Hilarious Riders. Their involvement in various causes sets them apart from the other motorcycle clubs that cruise the streets.
J’espère que vous aurez autant de plaisi: I hope you’ll enjoy reading this story as much as I enjoyed writing it.
<strong>Suzuki SV, Yamaha R7, Kawasaki N: Suzuki SV, Yamaha R7, Kawasaki Ninja: on this Saturday in mid-July, many motorcycles are lined up along the basketball court at Parc Don-Bosco, in Rivière-des-Prairies, for a tournament organized by the Hilarious Riders. We went to meet some of the members of this motorcycle club with a mission of solidarity. A portrait.
« <em>Hilarious Riders</em>, c’est un cl: “Hilarious Riders is a motorcycle club focused on charity work. It’s the only thing that sets us apart and it’s what gives us longevity. Motorcycle clubs come and go, because they don’t have that cornerstone that makes people want to keep investing themselves,” says Alberto Speech, a.k.a. Spook, the club’s vice-president.
Accoté à son Campagna T-Rex, habillé d’u: Leaning against his Campagna T-Rex, dressed in a leather tank top, with dark shades over his eyes and a gold chain around his neck, he exudes self-confidence.
« On veut montrer que c’est cool d’être: “We want to show that it’s cool to be ‘legit.’ I’ve got my J’s on my feet, my gold around my neck… To have stuff like that, you don’t have to be in the dirt. Everybody in the group works. Even if we look badass, we don’t do anything illegal!”
Lui-même porte de nombreux chapeaux. Pom: He wears many hats himself. A firefighter with the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal, he is a captain at the Montréal-Nord station. He also teaches fire safety techniques at Collège de Montmorency and works as a public speaker.
C’est cependant le rôle de militant impl: But it’s his role as an activist involved in the community that keeps him “the most motivated.”
Le club Hilarious Riders participe à un: The Hilarious Riders club takes part in a basketball tournament organized as part of the Festival Urbain de RDP (Rivière-des-Prairies) on July 12. The funds raised will go to a humanitarian mission in Africa. Photo credit: Ismaël Koné
« On a des programmes de parrainages de: “We have youth mentorship programs. Often single parents contact us because they’re having a hard time with their kid. We come meet them, we give them guidance, and we offer them activities with us,” says Alberto Speech.
Derrière lui, le tournoi de basket suit: Behind him, the basketball tournament carries on. The funds raised at the event will help finance orphanages in Togo and Benin, as part of a humanitarian mission the group will carry out in January 2026.
« C’est difficile d’être dans les <em>Hi: “It’s hard to be in the Hilarious Riders, because you have to give your time and energy to people you don’t know,” he explains. “What we ask is that you have your heart in the right place.”
Il rappelle à ce propos qu’il y a toujou: He adds that there are always new causes to defend, and that this is what motivates members to keep coming together.
Jeff Beaulieu, alias Mozbius est pour sa: Jeff Beaulieu, a.k.a. Mozbius, has been in the group since its very beginning. “I’m an ‘OG (Original Gangster),’” says the man who works in IT, laughing.
« C’est la réalisation d’un rêve. Au déb: “It’s a dream come true. In the beginning, we didn’t think about starting a motorcycle club. We started out as a group of friends who just wanted to have fun together, and then to share that fun with other people,” he recalls.
Peu à peu, le groupe a grandi, s’est str: Little by little, the group grew, became more structured, and turned into the club as it exists today, with its social mission as an integral part of its activities.
« Ce dont je suis le plus fier, c’est qu: “What I’m proudest of is that after 25 years, we’re still here,” Mozbius exclaims.
« On ne recrute pas, mais si des gens so: “We don’t recruit, but if people are interested in what we do, as we see them around, we can start the process,” explains Alberto Speech.
Un nouveau venu devient d’abord un « han: A newcomer first becomes a “hang around,” a role in which they are invited to take part in various club activities. It’s a time for observation. At the next stage, the person is promoted to “prospect,” a probationary period during which they must show their desire to become a full member. After a certain period of time, the process ends when the rider becomes a “full patch.” It’s a structure similar to that of many motorcycle clubs.
« On ne cherche pas à aller chercher le: “We’re not trying to get the maximum number of members. We want soldiers, people who will be here to stay and who understand what we do,” he adds.
Professionnelle en ressources humaines e: A human resources professional and founder of the organization Jeunes athlètes de Montréal (JAM), Fatou Camara was named one of the 100 most influential women in Canada in 2024 by the Women’s Executive Network. She recently joined the club as a “prospect,” having been drawn first and foremost by its community involvement. She cites the group’s values, including its family spirit and mutual aid, among the things that encouraged her to join.
“I’ve been riding for 15 years. I can go far fast on my own, but by joining the club, I feel a sense of belonging to something bigger than me,” says Fatou, resting against the seat of her Suzuki SV650.
« Je les ai rejoints parce que je voulai: “I joined them because I wanted to add my strength to the community,” she says.
Fatou Camara, une membre 'prospect' du c: Fatou Camara, a “prospect” member of the Hilarious Riders club. Photo credit: Ismaël Koné
Coach, qui tire son nom de la profession: Coach, who gets his name from his profession, joined the group only a year ago, although he has known several of its members for much longer. For him, the club has become a second family. What makes him proudest is being able to give back to the community.
« Les jeunes voient qu’il y a des groupe: “Young people see that there are motorcycle groups, that it’s not just the street gang thing, but that we’re here for a good cause. We want to give them a good image. We want young people to see that and recreate it in their future.”
De son côté, Ivy est dans le groupe depu: Ivy, for her part, has been in the group for more than 10 years now, serving as project manager. She discovered the Hilarious Riders at a blood drive organized for Héma-Québec.
« C’est là que j’ai vu l’implication que: “That’s where I saw how involved the group was in the community. It tapped into a humanitarian side that had always interested me, but that I couldn’t put into practice in my daily life.”
Un quart de siècle après sa fondation, l: A quarter of a century after its founding, the Hilarious Riders motorcycle club is still going, and its members are more involved than ever. They hope to keep revving their engines for a long time to come to move the community forward.
